what: Apple Silicon (M1 Pro) live measurement of the OS pointer under the engine's cursor capture (Mouse::refreshCursorCapture -> Win32Mouse::capture -> PlatformWindowHost::setCursorClip -> Cocoa Window_Set_Cursor_Clip), before and after the Wave 14 confinement fix in platform_window_cocoa.mm. Hand-written from the session's LLDB/HID output; not produced by a script.
platform: macOS 26.6.1 arm64 (Apple M1 Pro), 1728x1117 points at backing scale 2x, Apple clang 21.0.0, MoltenVK 1.4.2
binary: scripts/native-build.py --level 1 --level 2 --level 3 --level 4 --with-shims --strict-link: 981/981 objects, 0 undefined, strict link exit 0, build/native/native_strict_link Mach-O 64-bit arm64 (lipo -archs: arm64), run with arch -arm64

method.pointer_motion: IOHIDPostEvent(NX_MOUSEMOVED, kIOHIDSetRelativeCursorPosition) with dx/dy deltas - the HID-system entry a hardware mouse's deltas take, so CGAssociateMouseAndMouseCursorPosition(false) is honoured (validated in a standalone AppKit window: 0 px moved while dissociated, full delta after re-association). Absolute CGEvent posts, which #154 used, move the pointer regardless of association and therefore did NOT test motion under capture.
method.clicks: IOHIDPostEvent left button down/up at the CURRENT pointer location, no coordinates supplied
method.engine_state: LLDB attach to the running arm64 binary reading TheMouse->m_isCursorCaptured, WWPlatform::TheWindow->Cursor_Clipped, Window_Is_Active(), TheMouse->m_currMouse.pos, TheGameLogic->m_gameMode, TheInGameUI->m_isQuitMenuVisible; no OpenAL/AIL_* function evaluated from the debugger
method.focus_loss: osascript 'tell application Finder to activate', then NSRunningApplication activateWithOptions: to return
method.visibility: screencapture -C (cursor included) inspected by eye; screenshots are session artefacts, not committed

pre_fix.mechanism: Window_Set_Cursor_Clip(true) called CGAssociateMouseAndMouseCursorPosition(false): the pointer stops following the mouse whenever the engine has capture. PROVEN for the two states below where capture was on; the pointer stayed visible (retail arrow) in every state.

windowed_main_menu.verdict: MEASURED-WORKING (default CursorCaptureMode has no windowed-menu bit, so nothing was captured)

fullscreen_main_menu.verdict: FROZEN - mechanism confirmed; the borderless window was also never key (NSWindow canBecomeKeyWindow is NO for a borderless style mask), so AppKit delivered it no mouse-moved events

fix.confinement: Window_Set_Cursor_Clip records Cursor_Clipped only; every mouse-moved/dragged/button event that arrives outside the content view while clipped and active is clamped to [0,w-1]x[0,h-1] and the pointer warped there (CGWarpMouseCursorPosition + CGAssociateMouseAndMouseCursorPosition(true) to cancel the post-warp motion suppression). Cursor_Clipped(true) also pulls a pointer that is already outside onto the edge at once, as ClipCursor does. The pointer is never dissociated.
fix.key_window: WWGameWindow (NSWindow subclass) answers canBecomeKeyWindow/canBecomeMainWindow YES so the borderless fullscreen window is key and receives mouse-moved events, as a Win32 WS_POPUP window does.

windowed_unpaused_skirmish.hid_click_at_pointer: ButtonOptions (control bar) at engine 202,502 opened the quit menu

windowed_pause_menu.hid_click_at_pointer: ButtonReturn at engine 400,395 closed the quit menu; capture re-engaged (captured=1 clipped=1)

fullscreen_pause_menu.hid_click_at_pointer: ButtonReturn closed the quit menu; capture re-engaged

post_fix.cursor_visible: yes in every state above (retail arrow at menus; SCCScroll diagonal arrow when parked at the fullscreen window's bottom-right corner)

unmeasured: human confirmation on a real trackpad (exit criterion; the user's original main-menu report is UNEXPLAINED until he says windowed vs fullscreen and invisible/frozen/misclick)
the engine's 'fullscreen' on this Mac is an 800x600 borderless window at the top-left of the 1728x1117-point screen, not a screen-covering one - a window-mode seam, out of this slice
first mouse event after re-activation reaches the engine clamped to (800,600) before the warp pulls the pointer to (799,599); harmless, Windows clamps the same way
hide-on-cinematic, button-edge click, seven of eight scroll cursor directions, dragging with a button held across the edge, multi-display
